root_cause.text: Synchronous FUSE_INIT made the mounting thread wait inside a recursive FUSE request while still holding the device file open, but the request was marked FR_FORCE and had no fatal-signal abort path, so server death during init could not trigger connection abort and the mount hung.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that in sync init “the mounting thread … will keep the device fd open, which will prevent an abort from happening,” and the patch adds `abort_on_kill` for `fuse_send_init()`, makes `request_wait_answer()` call `fuse_abort_conn(fc)` when that flag is set, and avoids setting `FR_FORCE` when `abort_on_kill` is enabled.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: Synchronous FUSE_INIT made the mounting thread wait inside a recursive FUSE request while still holding the device file open, but the request was marked FR_FORCE and had no fatal-signal abort path, so server death during init could not trigger connection abort and the mount hung.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message states that in sync init “the mounting thread … will keep the device fd open, which will prevent an abort from happening,” and the patch adds `abort_on_kill` for `fuse_send_init()`, makes `request_wait_answer()` call `fuse_abort_conn(fc)` when that flag is set, and avoids setting `FR_FORCE` when `abort_on_kill` is enabled.

intent_record.intent_summary: Abort the FUSE connection immediately for requests flagged abort_on_kill when request_wait_answer() exits with an error.
intent_record.what: A new conditional block was added in request_wait_answer() after the error check: if req->args->abort_on_kill is true, it calls fuse_abort_conn(fc) and returns immediately before the existing FR_URING/non-FR_URING pending-request removal logic.
intent_record.how: At runtime, requests marked with abort_on_kill now trigger an immediate FUSE connection abort when the wait path encounters an error instead of continuing with normal pending-request cleanup handling. This changes killed/interrupted request handling so the entire connection is torn down promptly for those requests.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid forcing FUSE requests that should abort on kill so killable operations can be interrupted correctly.
intent_record.what: The unconditional setting of the FR_FORCE flag on req->flags in the synchronous request path was changed to be conditional on args->abort_on_kill being false, by wrapping __set_bit(FR_FORCE, &req->flags) in an if (!args->abort_on_kill) check.
intent_record.how: At runtime, requests marked with abort_on_kill will no longer be forced with FR_FORCE, allowing them to be interrupted or aborted when the task is killed instead of being treated as uninterruptible forced requests; requests without abort_on_kill keep the previous behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an abort_on_kill flag to fuse_args so FUSE requests can carry kill-abort behavior metadata.
intent_record.what: A new one-bit boolean field named abort_on_kill was added to struct fuse_args immediately after the existing invalidate_vmap bitfield.
intent_record.how: This extends the fuse_args data structure so code using it can record whether an operation should be aborted when a kill-related condition occurs, enabling later runtime logic to check and act on that flag.

intent_record.intent_summary: Mark synchronous FUSE init requests to abort on kill so killed tasks do not remain blocked during initialization.
intent_record.what: Within fuse_send_init(), inside the existing `if (fm->fc->sync_init)` branch, the code adds one new statement before `fuse_simple_request(fm, &ia->args);`: `ia->args.abort_on_kill = true;`.
intent_record.how: This causes the synchronous FUSE init request to be marked so it will be aborted if the task is killed while waiting, instead of continuing to block in the request path. At runtime, this changes synchronous initialization behavior to be interruptible by a fatal kill condition.

grouping_result.intent: Mark synchronous FUSE init requests to abort on kill so killed tasks do not remain blocked during initialization.
Add an abort_on_kill flag to fuse_args so FUSE requests can carry kill-abort behavior metadata.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure killable/synchronous FUSE initialization requests are marked and handled to abort promptly on fatal signals so tasks do not remain blocked.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly target the root cause: synchronous FUSE_INIT requests were forced and lacked a fatal-signal abort path, causing mount hangs when the server died. This group makes init requests abort-on-kill, avoids forcing such requests, and aborts the connection on wait errors, which addresses the blocked mount behavior.

The root cause is that the synchronous FUSE_INIT request lacked a fatal-signal/kill abort path. Adding an abort_on_kill flag to fuse_args directly introduces metadata needed for requests to support kill-triggered abort behavior, which addresses that core issue.

candidates.rationale: This synchronous FUSE_INIT request was issued without any abort-on-kill metadata, causing the mounting task to block in request wait with no fatal-signal escape path during init.

Marking the request FR_FORCE prevented normal interrupt/abort behavior, which is central to the hang: the init request became unabortable even when the server died or the task received a fatal signal.

vuln_statements.explanation: This synchronous FUSE_INIT request submission is the direct trigger of the hang: it waited for completion during mount, but the request lacked abort-on-kill handling, so if the server died during initialization the mounting task remained blocked.

Setting FR_FORCE made the request uninterruptible with respect to the needed abort path. In combination with the synchronous init request, this prevented fatal-signal-driven interruption/connection abort and allowed the mount to hang when the server died.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it directly shows the new synchronous FUSE_INIT path and how the init request is issued. In `fuse_new_init()`, the request is explicitly marked forced: `ia->args.force = true;` and `ia->args.nocreds = true;`. In the new `fuse_send_init(struct fuse_mount *fm)`, the synchronous path is added: `if (fm->fc->sync_init) { err = fuse_simple_request(fm, &ia->args); ... }`. This matches the root cause: a synchronous FUSE_INIT is now performed by the mounting thread. There is no visible handling here for aborting that forced synchronous request on fatal signal or server death; instead the code simply waits via `fuse_simple_request()` on a request that was created with `force = true`. The old asynchronous path used `fuse_simple_background(...)`, but the new sync path blocks in-request. The later `process_init_reply(fm, &ia->args, err); if (fm->fc->conn_error) return -ENOTCONN;` only runs after `fuse_simple_request()` returns, so it does not provide an escape path from the wait itself. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present: synchronous init plus forced request without an abort path. The fix is not present in this function body/diff.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
fuse: introduce fuse_simple_request() helper

The following pattern is repeated many times:

	req = fuse_get_req_nopages
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the full new helper used for synchronous FUSE requests. The root cause is that synchronous FUSE_INIT used a request path that waited while lacking the special abort handling needed when the request is forced. This helper performs a plain synchronous send: `fuse_request_send(fc, req);` and then waits for completion/result via `ret = req->out.h.error;`. The request is allocated with `req = fuse_get_req(fc, 0);`, i.e. with no special flags visible here, and there is no logic in this helper for fatal-signal interruption, no special handling for forced init requests, and no connection-abort escape path if the userspace server dies during init. The function simply sends, reads `req->out.h.error`, optionally returns variable output size, and `fuse_put_request(fc, req);`. Therefore the vulnerable synchronous request construct is present, and the fix is not present in this function.
